page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine designed for compute-skewed infrastructure demands, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor delivering 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading at a clock frequency of 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large shared 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced execution instruction sets, including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8), facilitating hardware-accelerated numeric computation.

System memory totals 128.0 GB, which establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration deliberately trades high memory capacity for compute density, making it cost-efficient for workloads that do not demand expansive per-thread footprints. There is no bundled local storage on the instance, nor are there integrated GPU accelerators. Consequently, persistence and high-IOPS data handling must be provisioned via remote block storage networks, and graphics or tensor processing is limited strictly to the CPU subsystem.

Empirical benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing capability, with the instance scoring 87,182.31 on PassMark CPU tests and exhibiting strong stress-ng multi-threaded throughput. Memory bandwidth exceeds 326 GB/s on large uncached read transfers and 128 GB/s on write transfers, translating to over 113 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 89.08 GB/s in static web serving benchmarks. Single-core execution falls closer to median thresholds across stress tests. Given these operational metrics, the D64ls_v7 is tailored for batch processing, parallel compilation, high-volume web serving, data compression, and CPU-based machine learning prompt evaluation.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine driven by a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory. Operating on a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance directs resources toward CPU-intensive tasks rather than memory capacity. The processor incorporates an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Synthetic benchmarks place the multi-core CPU throughput in the top ten percent, backed by high memory bandwidth and resilient Redis and web-serving performance. Because the instance contains zero integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, workloads rely entirely on external network storage. With its compute-dense hardware layout, the instance provides efficient scaling for high-throughput batch computation, web application serving, compression tasks, and CPU-driven inference pipelines that do not require massive per-core memory allocations.
